## Initializing

```{r}
#| include: false
require(pacman)
p_load(tidyverse,    janitor,     parsedate, sjPlot,
       lubridate,    cowplot,    purrr,  readr,      googledrive,    zoo,
       dplyr,     stringr,     purrr,  googlesheets4,      arrow,      ggplot2,
       ggpubr,     data.table,   patchwork,    sjPlot, Metrics,   
       yardstick,   lme4,   ggpmisc, Matrix, rlang,    scales,   here,
       pdp,   sf,   maps, tibble,lmerTest, MuMIn, broom.mixed)

# Set ggplot theme
theme_set(theme_bw())

# ---- Data folder: defined ONCE here ------------------------------------------------
# Every input file is read with dfile("file name"), so no chunk depends on the working
# directory (RStudio uses the .qmd folder when running chunks and the project folder in
# the console, which is why bai_data_OWC.csv was found in one and not in the other).
# The folder is found automatically: the first of these that contains df_root_flux_2026.rds:
# the folder of this .qmd, the working directory, the project root (here::here()), or any
# subfolder of the project root. To set it by hand, replace NULL with the path, e.g.
# data_dir <- "D:/GitHub/GHG_LE_soil_trees/scripts"
data_dir <- NULL
key_file <- "df_root_flux_2026.rds"

if (is.null(data_dir)) {
  qmd_dir <- tryCatch(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), error = function(e) character(0))
  if (length(qmd_dir) == 0 && requireNamespace("rstudioapi", quietly = TRUE) && rstudioapi::isAvailable())
    qmd_dir <- tryCatch(dirname(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path), error = function(e) character(0))
  cands <- unique(c(qmd_dir, getwd(), here::here()))
  hit   <- cands[file.exists(file.path(cands, key_file))]
  if (length(hit) == 0)
    hit <- dirname(list.files(here::here(), pattern = paste0("^", key_file, "$"),
                              recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE))
  if (length(hit) == 0) stop("Could not find ", key_file, ": set data_dir by hand at the top of the script.")
  data_dir <- hit[1]
}
data_dir <- normalizePath(data_dir, winslash = "/")
message("Data folder: ", data_dir)

# Path of an input file: data_dir first, then the project root. must_exist = FALSE returns
# the path in data_dir for files the script creates itself (downloads saved once).
dfile <- function(name, must_exist = TRUE) {
  cands <- file.path(unique(c(data_dir, here::here())), name)
  hit   <- cands[file.exists(cands)]
  if (length(hit) > 0) return(hit[1])
  if (must_exist) stop("File not found: ", name, "\n  looked in: ",
                       paste(dirname(cands), collapse = " | "), call. = FALSE)
  file.path(data_dir, name)
}

# Data kept outside the project (other drives): paths set here, in one place.
compass_dir <- "D:/COMPASS_L2-v2-1"
nut_file    <- "C:/Users/rbitten/OneDrive - University of Toledo/Documents/Multiplexer/Nutrients/raw_data_AQ700/nutrients_combined.csv"
```

## Preparing df's

```{r}


# reading flux, sap, and L1 data created and QAQCedin a separated script
df_root_flux_2026 <- readRDS(dfile("df_root_flux_2026.rds"))
#df_ALL_sap_Js <- readRDS("df_ALL_sap_Js.rds")
df_L1_root <- readRDS(dfile("df_L1_root.rds"))
df_sap_OWC<-readRDS(dfile("df_sap_OWC.rds")) # created after QAQC all synoptic sites

# merging gw, vpd with sap FOR FIG 2
df_sap_OWC <- readRDS(dfile("df_sap_OWC.rds")) %>%
  mutate(
    TIMESTAMP = ymd_hms(TIMESTAMP),
    F = replace(F, !is.finite(F), NA_real_),
    datetime = floor_date(TIMESTAMP, "hour")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    Plot == "TR",
    TIMESTAMP > as.POSIXct("2024-03-25 00:00:00"),
    TIMESTAMP < as.POSIXct("2025-05-15 00:00:00")
  ) %>%
  group_by(datetime, Site, Plot, Sensor_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      where(is.numeric),
      ~ if (all(!is.finite(.x))) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        mean(.x[is.finite(.x)])
      }
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Exclude unreliable sap flow:
#   - winter months (sensors not maintained): Nov, Dec, Jan
#   - bad data from 14 Oct 2024 until the end of that winter
sap_bad_months <- c(11, 12, 1)
sap_bad_start  <- as.POSIXct("2024-10-14 00:00:00", tz = lubridate::tz(df_sap_OWC$datetime))
sap_bad_end    <- as.POSIXct("2025-06-01 00:00:00", tz = lubridate::tz(df_sap_OWC$datetime))

sap_is_bad <- function(datetime) {
  month(datetime) %in% sap_bad_months | (datetime >= sap_bad_start & datetime < sap_bad_end)
}

df_sap_OWC <- df_sap_OWC %>%
  mutate(F = if_else(sap_is_bad(datetime), NA_real_, F))

#df_L1_sap_vps_gw<-df_ALL_sap_Js%>%left_join(df_L1_root, by = "datetime")
df_L1_sap_vps_gw<-df_sap_OWC%>%left_join(df_L1_root, by = "datetime")

df_L1_sap_vps_gw<-df_L1_sap_vps_gw%>%
  mutate(gw_hour=100*gwl_median,              # transforming m to cm
         DATE = as.Date(datetime, format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
         DOY = yday(datetime))

# merging gw, vpd with sap dfs for RF

df_L1_datetime<- df_L1_sap_vps_gw %>%
  select(-Sensor_ID) %>%
  group_by(datetime) %>%
  summarise(
    across(where(is.numeric), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    across(where(~ !is.numeric(.x)), ~ first(.x)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

df_L1_filtered<-df_L1_datetime%>%dplyr::select(-c(DATE,DOY))

df_flux_hour<-df_root_flux_2026%>%left_join(df_L1_filtered, by = "datetime")

L1_flux<-df_flux_hour%>%mutate(season = case_when(
      DATE >= as.Date("2024-03-20") & DATE < as.Date("2024-06-22") ~ "Spring",
      DATE >= as.Date("2024-06-22") & DATE < as.Date("2024-09-24") ~ "Summer",
      DATE >= as.Date("2024-09-24") & DATE < as.Date("2024-12-22") ~ "Fall",
      DATE >= as.Date("2024-12-22") & DATE < as.Date("2025-03-20") ~ "Winter",
      DATE >= as.Date("2025-03-20") & DATE < as.Date("2025-06-22") ~ "Spring",
      DATE >= as.Date("2025-06-22") & DATE < as.Date("2025-09-24") ~ "Summer"
    ))


# =====================================================
# DIAGNOSING AND REMOVING BAD TEMPERATURE RECORDS IN JULY
# =====================================================

# ---- 1) Diagnostic: confirm failure window in July, overall ----
ts_july_fail_check <- L1_flux %>%
  filter(month(datetime) == 7, TS_1 <= 1) %>%
  arrange(datetime) %>%
  summarise(first_bad = min(datetime), last_bad = max(datetime), n = n())

print(ts_july_fail_check)

# ---- 2) Same, broken down by PORT (window varies slightly: PORT 3 ends earlier) ----
ts_july_fail_by_port <- L1_flux %>%
  filter(month(datetime) == 7, TS_1 <= 1) %>%
  group_by(PORT) %>%
  summarise(first_bad = min(datetime), last_bad = max(datetime), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(PORT)

print(ts_july_fail_by_port)

# ---- 3) Visual check: raw TS_1 by PORT, black = all data, red = flagged ----
p_ts_raw_port <- ggplot(L1_flux, aes(x = datetime, y = TS_1)) +
  geom_point(color = "black", alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
  geom_point(
    data = L1_flux %>% filter(TS_1 <= 1),
    color = "red", size = 1
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ PORT, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Datetime", y = "Soil Temp - TS_1 (°C, raw)",
       title = "Raw soil temperature by PORT",
       subtitle = "Red = points with TS_1 <= 1") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 14),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(p_ts_raw_port)

# ---- 4) Clean L1_flux: NA out TS_1 for the confirmed July failure window ----
# Using the overall window (2024-07-11 10:00 to 2024-07-31 15:00), which
# safely covers every PORT's individual failure window (PORT 3 recovers
# earlier, on 2024-07-24, so it's simply unaffected after that date).
ts_fail_start <- ts_july_fail_check$first_bad
ts_fail_end   <- ts_july_fail_check$last_bad

L1_flux <- L1_flux %>%
  mutate(
    TS_1_flag = if_else(datetime >= ts_fail_start & datetime <= ts_fail_end &
                          TS_1 <= 1,
                        "sensor_failure_july", "ok"),
    TS_1 = if_else(TS_1_flag == "sensor_failure_july", NA_real_, TS_1)
  )

# ---- 5) Confirm cleaning worked ----
L1_flux %>%
  filter(TS_1_flag == "sensor_failure_july") %>%
  summarise(n_flagged = n(), first = min(datetime), last = max(datetime))

# Should return zero
L1_flux %>%
  filter(month(datetime) == 7, TS_1 <= 1) %>%
  nrow()

#averaging data per date-hour and treatment
df_summary_hour <- L1_flux%>%
  group_by(datetime,
           Treat, 
           season) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean_FCH4 = mean((FCH4), na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_FCH4 = sd((FCH4), na.rm = TRUE),
            median_FCH4 = median((FCH4), na.rm = TRUE),
            IQR_FCH4 = IQR((FCH4), na.rm = TRUE),
            
            mean_SWC = mean((SWC_1), na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_SWC = sd((SWC_1), na.rm = TRUE),
            median_SWC = median((SWC_1), na.rm = TRUE),
            IQR_SWC = IQR((SWC_1), na.rm = TRUE),
            
            mean_TS = mean((TS_1), na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_TS = sd((TS_1), na.rm = TRUE),
            median_TS = median((TS_1), na.rm = TRUE),
            IQR_TS = IQR((TS_1), na.rm = TRUE),
           
            mean_FCO2 = mean((FCO2), na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_FCO2 = sd((FCO2), na.rm = TRUE),
            median_FCO2 = median((FCO2), na.rm = TRUE),
            IQR_FCO2 = IQR((FCO2), na.rm = TRUE),
            
            mean_gwl = mean((gwl_median), na.rm = TRUE), #cm
            sd_gwl = sd((gwl_median), na.rm = TRUE),
            median_gwl = median((gwl_median), na.rm = TRUE),
            IQR_gwl = IQR((gwl_median), na.rm = TRUE),
            
            # mean_sap =  mean(Js_kgcms, na.rm = TRUE),
            # sd_sap =  sd(Js_kgcms, na.rm = TRUE),
            # median_sap =  median(Js_kgcms, na.rm = TRUE),
            # IQR_sap=IQR(Js_kgcms, na.rm = TRUE),
            
            mean_sap =  mean(F, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_sap =  sd(F, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_sap =  median(F, na.rm = TRUE),
            IQR_sap=IQR(F, na.rm = TRUE),
            
            mean_vpd = mean((VPD_hour), na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_vpd = sd((VPD_hour), na.rm = TRUE),
            median_vpd = median((VPD_hour), na.rm = TRUE),
            IQR_vpd = IQR((VPD_hour), na.rm = TRUE),
            n_obs = n()
                ) %>%
             ungroup()

df_rain<-df_L1_datetime%>%dplyr::select(rain_sum, datetime)

df_gamm<-df_summary_hour%>%left_join(df_rain, by="datetime")
```

## Fig 3 - CH4 SWC boxplot

```{r}
make_boxplot <- function(df, season_name, var, ylab = NULL, ylim_vals = NULL, 
                         show_title = FALSE, xlabels = NULL, y_pval = NULL,
                         panel_label = NULL, hline = NULL) {
  
  df_season <- df %>%
    filter(season == season_name,
           Treat %in% c("Root-free", "Control")) %>%
    mutate(Treat = factor(Treat, levels = c("Root-free", "Control"))) %>%
    select(datetime, Treat, value = {{ var }}) %>%
    group_by(datetime) %>%
    filter(n_distinct(Treat) == 2) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  df_wide <- df_season %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Treat,
                values_from = value,
                values_fn = median)
  
  pval <- wilcox.test(df_wide$Control, df_wide$`Root-free`,
                      paired = TRUE)$p.value
  
  if (is.null(y_pval)) {
    y_pval <- min(df_season$value, na.rm = TRUE) +
      0.05 * diff(range(df_season$value, na.rm = TRUE))
  }
  
  g <- ggplot(df_season, aes(x = Treat, y = value, fill = Treat)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, color = "black", alpha = 0.9) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.8, y = y_pval,
             label = paste0("p = ", signif(pval, 3)),
             size = 5, hjust = 0) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Root-free" = "#440154FF",
                                 "Control"   = "#7AD151FF")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab, title = if (show_title) season_name) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      text = element_text(size = 20),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16)
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = xlabels)
  
  if (!is.null(hline)) {
    g <- g + geom_hline(yintercept = hline,
                        linetype = "dashed",
                        color = "darkgray")
  }
  
  if (!is.null(panel_label)) {
    g <- g +
      annotate("text",
               x = -Inf, y = Inf,
               label = panel_label,
               hjust = -0.3, vjust = 1.2,
               size = 6)
  }
  
  if (!is.null(ylim_vals)) g <- g + coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim_vals)
  
  return(g)
}
```

## Prep df for CH4 cumulative flux

```{r}

# to calculate it per PORT use L1_flux df 
# to calculate it per Treat use df_summary_hour
#--------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare data: ensure we use the same time period for the other anaysis
#--------------------------------------------------
L1_fluxsummary <- df_summary_hour%>%
  filter(datetime<="2025-01-14 16:00:00"&datetime>="2024-04-05 15:00:00",
          median_FCH4<250&median_FCH4>-250)%>% #removing outliers - limit detection issues??
  mutate(median_FCH4=median_FCH4*3600) #converting second to hour
#--------------------------------------------------
# 2. Full datetime × PORT grid
#--------------------------------------------------
start_time <- as.POSIXct("2024-04-05 15:00:00")
end_time   <- as.POSIXct("2025-04-05 14:00:00")

all_hours <- tibble(datetime = seq(from = start_time, to = end_time, by = "1 hour"))
#all_ports <- tibble(PORT = 1:8)
#full_grid <- crossing(all_ports, all_hours)
all_treat <- tibble(Treat = c("Control", "Root-free"))
full_grid <- crossing(all_treat, all_hours)

L1_flux_complete <- full_grid %>%
  left_join(L1_fluxsummary, by = c("Treat",#"PORT", 
                                   "datetime"))  %>%
  arrange(Treat, #PORT, 
          datetime) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(datetime),
         month = month(datetime))

#--------------------------------------------------
# 3. Linear interpolation < 24h
#--------------------------------------------------
L1_flux_complete <- L1_flux_complete %>%
  group_by(Treat#PORT
           ) %>%
  arrange(datetime) %>%
  mutate(FCH4_linear = na.approx(median_FCH4, x = datetime, maxgap = 23, na.rm = FALSE)) %>%
  ungroup()

#--------------------------------------------------
# 4. Monthly median by PORT
#--------------------------------------------------
monthly_median <- L1_flux_complete %>%
  group_by(Treat, #PORT, 
           month) %>%
  summarise(med_FCH4 = median(median_FCH4, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Treat #PORT
           ) %>%
  arrange(month) %>%
  mutate(
    # replicate month 1 median for month 2 if missing
    med_FCH4 = if_else(is.na(med_FCH4) & month == 2, med_FCH4[month == 1], med_FCH4)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

#--------------------------------------------------
# 5. Fill remaining gaps with monthly median
#--------------------------------------------------
L1_flux_complete <- L1_flux_complete %>%
  left_join(monthly_median, by = c("Treat",
                                    #"PORT", 
                                   "month")) %>%
  mutate(FCH4_GP = ifelse(is.na(FCH4_linear), med_FCH4, FCH4_linear),
    #--------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Create flag: 0 = observed, 1 = linear, 2 = monthly median
    #--------------------------------------------------
    gap_flag = case_when(
      !is.na(median_FCH4) ~ 0,
      is.na(median_FCH4) & !is.na(FCH4_linear) ~ 1,
      is.na(median_FCH4) & is.na(FCH4_linear) ~ 2
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-FCH4_linear, -med_FCH4)

#--------------------------------------------------
# 7. Plot for a specific PORT (e.g., PORT 1)
#--------------------------------------------------
ggplot(L1_flux_complete, 
       aes(x = datetime, y = FCH4_GP, color = factor(gap_flag), group=Treat))+#PORT)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("0" = "black", "1" = "blue", "2" = "red"),
    labels = c("0" = "Observed", "1" = "Linear interpolation", "2" = "Monthly median"),
    name = "Data type"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Datetime", y = expression(FCH[4]~"(umol m^-2 h^-1)"),
       title = "CH4 flux with gap filling") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")+facet_wrap(~Treat)

################# calcualting cumulative flux per port

# Assuming L1_flux_complete already has FCH4_GP filled
L1_flux_cumulative <- L1_flux_complete %>%
    mutate(Treat = factor(Treat)) %>%                 
    arrange(Treat, datetime) %>%                      
    group_by(Treat) %>%                               
    arrange(datetime, .by_group = TRUE) %>%           
    mutate(FCH4_cum = cumsum(replace_na(FCH4_GP, 0))) %>%  
    ungroup()


# Check result
head(L1_flux_cumulative)

ggplot(L1_flux_cumulative, aes(x = datetime, y = FCH4_cum, color = factor(Treat)))+#PORT))) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression("Cumulative " * FCH[4] * " (umol m^-2)"),
    title = "Cumulative CH4 flux over time - Control treatment",
    color = "Treat"#"PORT"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")+facet_wrap(~Treat)

# 8760 datetimes for each Treat but only 8016 FCH4 - missing days in March (and Feb) 744/24 = 31 days
 #L1_flux_complete %>%
   L1_flux_cumulative%>%
     group_by(Treat) %>%
    summarise(n = sum(!is.na(datetime),
              maxFCH4_cum= max(FCH4_cum),
              minFCH4_cum= min(FCH4_cum)), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# ---- Month levels for faceting (columns) ----
month_levels <- c("July", "August", "September", "October")

treatment_colors <- c("Control" = "#7AD151FF", "Root-free" = "#440154FF")

# ---- Climatology base: hour-of-day median per month, per Treat ----
df_climatology <- df_one_year %>%
  mutate(month = lubridate::month(datetime, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE),
         hour  = lubridate::hour(datetime)) %>%
  filter(month %in% month_levels) %>%
  mutate(month = factor(month, levels = month_levels))

ch4_summary <- df_climatology %>%
  group_by(month, hour, Treat) %>%
  summarise(median_val = median(median_FCH4, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

swc_summary <- df_climatology %>%
  group_by(month, hour, Treat) %>%
  summarise(median_val = median(median_SWC, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

ts_summary <- df_climatology %>%
  group_by(month, hour, Treat) %>%
  summarise(median_val = median(median_TS, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

# ---- Sap flow: no Treat split, black point / gray smooth ----
sap_summary <- df_sap_OWC %>%
  mutate(month = lubridate::month(datetime, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE),
         hour  = lubridate::hour(datetime)) %>%
  filter(month %in% month_levels) %>%
  mutate(month = factor(month, levels = month_levels)) %>%
  group_by(month, hour) %>%
  summarise(median_val = median(F, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

# ---- Generic hourly panel builder ----
make_hourly_plot <- function(df, ylab, treatment = TRUE,
                             show_x_axis = FALSE, show_strip = FALSE,
                             ylim_vals = NULL, y_breaks = NULL) {
  
  if (treatment) {
    g <- ggplot(df, aes(x = hour, y = median_val, color = Treat, fill = Treat)) +
      geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, alpha = 0.2) +
      geom_point(size = 2) +
      scale_color_manual(values = treatment_colors, name = "Treatment") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = treatment_colors, name = "Treatment")
  } else {
    g <- ggplot(df, aes(x = hour, y = median_val)) +
      geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE,
                  color = "black", fill = "gray50", alpha = 0.3) +
      geom_point(color = "black", size = 2)
  }
  
  g <- g +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(9, 15), linetype = "dotted",
               color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~ month, nrow = 1) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 21, by = 3), limits = c(0, 23)) +
    labs(x = if (show_x_axis) "Hour of day" else NULL, y = ylab) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      text = element_text(size = 18),
      axis.text.x = if (show_x_axis) element_text(size = 14) else element_blank(),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black"),
      strip.text = if (show_strip) element_text(size = 16, face = "bold") else element_blank()
    )
  
  if (!is.null(ylim_vals)) g <- g + coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim_vals)
  if (!is.null(y_breaks))  g <- g + scale_y_continuous(breaks = y_breaks)
  
  return(g)
}

# ---- Build the 4 rows ----
p_ch4 <- make_hourly_plot(
  ch4_summary,
  ylab = bquote(atop("CH"[4] ~ "flux", ~ mu*mol ~ m^{-2} ~ s^{-1})),
  treatment = TRUE, show_x_axis = FALSE, show_strip = TRUE,
  ylim_vals = c(-2, 0.3)
)

p_swc <- make_hourly_plot(
  swc_summary,
  ylab = bquote(atop("Soil moisture", ~m^3 ~ m^{-3})),
  treatment = TRUE, show_x_axis = FALSE, show_strip = FALSE,
  y_breaks = seq(0, 0.55, by = 0.1)
)

p_ts <- make_hourly_plot(
  ts_summary,
  ylab = "Soil Temp \n°C",
  treatment = TRUE, show_x_axis = FALSE, show_strip = FALSE,
  ylim_vals = c(10, 25)
)

p_sap <- make_hourly_plot(
  sap_summary,
  ylab = bquote(atop("Sapflow", ~kg ~ m^{-2} ~ s^{-1})),
  treatment = FALSE, show_x_axis = TRUE, show_strip = FALSE,
  y_breaks = seq(0, 0.0025, by = 0.001)
)

# ---- Combine with a single collected, horizontal top legend ----
Fig_hourly <- p_ch4 / p_swc / p_ts / p_sap +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank())

print(Fig_hourly)

ggsave(
  filename = "fig_hourly_climatologyB.png",

  width = 14,

  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```

```{r}
# =========================================================
# Settings
# =========================================================
date_end <- as.Date("2025-01-20")

# Treatment colors 
treatment_colors <- c("Control" = "#7AD151FF", "Root-free" = "#440154FF")

# If you want the SAME colors for fill and line, just reuse the same vector:
treatment_colors_line <- treatment_colors
treatment_colors_fill <- treatment_colors

# =========================================================
# 1) Median per hour (from L1_flux)
# =========================================================
summary_stats_hour <- L1_flux %>%
  mutate(
    datehour = as.POSIXct(datetime),                    
    hour     = as.numeric(format(datehour, "%H")),
    month    = factor(format(datehour, "%b"), levels = month.abb),
    DATE     = as.Date(datehour)
  ) %>%
  group_by(DATE, datehour, month, hour, Treat) %>%
  summarise(
    median_FCH4  = median(FCH4, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_FCO2  = median(FCO2, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_SWC_1 = median(SWC_1, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_TS_1  = median(TS_1, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_gwl   = median(gwl_median, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_sap   = median(F, na.rm = TRUE),

    # rain: use max per hour to avoid multiplying rain across PORT replicates
    sum_rain     = suppressWarnings(max(rain_sum, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(sum_rain = ifelse(is.infinite(sum_rain), NA_real_, sum_rain))%>%filter(!(month == "Jul" &  median_TS_1 <= 5))

# =========================================================
# 2) Monthly summary (median + Q1/Q3) by month x hour x treatment
# =========================================================
mensal_median <- summary_stats_hour %>%
  filter(DATE <= date_end) %>%
  group_by(month, hour, Treat) %>%
  summarise(
    median_CH4 = median(median_FCH4, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1_CH4     = quantile(median_FCH4, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3_CH4     = quantile(median_FCH4, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),

    median_FCO2 = median(median_FCO2, na.rm = TRUE),

    Q3_swc     = quantile(median_SWC_1, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),

    median_temp = median(median_TS_1, na.rm = TRUE),

    # total rain per month for each hour-of-day (sum of hourly maxima)

# =========================================================
# 3) Function: plot variable by treatment (colored)
# =========================================================
plot_variable <- function(df, yvar, y1 = NA, y2 = NA, y_label = NULL,
                          show_months = FALSE, show_x = FALSE) {

  df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[yvar]]), !is.na(month))

  base_name <- sub("median_", "", yvar)
  ymin_var  <- paste0("Q1_", base_name)
  ymax_var  <- paste0("Q3_", base_name)

  y_limits <- if (is.na(y1) | is.na(y2)) NULL else c(y1, y2)

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = hour, y = !!sym(yvar), color = Treat, fill = Treat)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 19, xmax = 24, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.4, linetype = "dashed") +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.4, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "black") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(5, 19), linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgrey") +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = !!sym(ymin_var), ymax = !!sym(ymax_var)),
                alpha = 0.25, color = NA) +
    geom_line(size = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = treatment_colors_line) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = treatment_colors_fill) +
    facet_wrap(~ month, ncol = 12, strip.position = "top") +
    labs(
      x = if (show_x) "Time of day (hour)" else NULL,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.title.x = if (show_x) element_text() else element_blank(),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text.x  = if (show_x) element_text() else element_blank(),
      strip.text   = if (show_months) element_text(size = 10) else element_blank()
    )

  if (!is.null(y_limits)) p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = y_limits)
  p
}

# =========================================================
# 4) Function: plot one treatment only (fixed gray)
# =========================================================
plot_single_treatment <- function(df, yvar, treat_keep = "Control",
                                  y1 = NA, y2 = NA, y_label = NULL,
                                  show_months = FALSE, show_x = FALSE) {

  df <- df %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[yvar]]), !is.na(month), Treat == treat_keep) %>%
    group_by(month, hour) %>%
    summarise(
      median = median(.data[[yvar]], na.rm = TRUE),
      Q1     = quantile(.data[[yvar]], 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      Q3     = quantile(.data[[yvar]], 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  y_limits <- if (is.na(y1) | is.na(y2)) NULL else c(y1, y2)

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = hour, y = median)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 19, xmax = 24, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.4, linetype = "dashed") +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.4, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "black") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(5, 19), linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgrey") +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q1, ymax = Q3), fill = "darkgray", alpha = 0.25) +
    geom_line(color = "darkgray", size = 1) +
    geom_point(color = "darkgray", size = 1.8) +
    facet_wrap(~ month, ncol = 12, strip.position = "top") +
    labs(
      x = if (show_x) "Time of day (hour)" else NULL,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.title.x = if (show_x) element_text() else element_blank(),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text.x  = if (show_x) element_text() else element_blank(),
      strip.text   = if (show_months) element_text(size = 10) else element_blank()
    )

  if (!is.null(y_limits)) p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = y_limits)
  p
}
```

## Fig S2 - Mixed Effect model

```{r}
# Daily CH4 per port explained by temperature, soil moisture, water table, VPD, rain and
# sap flux, with port and day as random effects, fitted separately for each treatment.
# Two models per treatment, because sap flux is only valid Apr to 13 Oct 2024:
#   A (no sap flux): all days with CH4 and environmental data, including Oct-Jan.
#   B (with sap flux): only days with valid sap flux.
# This keeps the Oct-Jan days instead of discarding them only because sap flux is missing.
# Coefficients are within-treatment associations, which mix all seasonal drivers; whether
# roots change the CH4 response to transpiration is tested in "Direct test".

# One row per port and day. Missing values are kept here and removed per model below.
df_mixed <- L1_flux %>%
  mutate(Date = as.Date(datetime)) %>%
  group_by(Date, Treat, PORT) %>%
  summarise(FCH4    = median(FCH4, na.rm = TRUE),
            SapFlow = median(F, na.rm = TRUE),
            Rain    = sum(rain_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
            Temp    = median(TS_1, na.rm = TRUE),
            SWC     = median(SWC_1, na.rm = TRUE),
            GWL     = median(gwl_median, na.rm = TRUE),
            VPD     = median(VPD_hour, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ if_else(is.finite(.x), .x, NA_real_)),   # median of all-NA gives NaN
         Treat = factor(Treat), PORT = factor(PORT))

cont_vars <- c("FCH4", "SapFlow", "Rain", "Temp", "SWC", "GWL", "VPD")
model_forms <- list(
  `A no sap flux`   = FCH4 ~ Temp + SWC + GWL + VPD + Rain + (1 | PORT) + (1 | Date),
  `B with sap flux` = FCH4 ~ Temp + SWC + GWL + VPD + SapFlow + Rain + (1 | PORT) + (1 | Date))

# Each model drops missing values only in its own variables, then standardizes within its
# own sample, so coefficients are per SD of that sample.
model_list <- list()
model_n    <- list()
for (tr in levels(df_mixed$Treat)) {
  for (m in names(model_forms)) {
    df_sub <- df_mixed %>%
      filter(Treat == tr) %>%
      tidyr::drop_na(all_of(all.vars(model_forms[[m]]))) %>%
      mutate(across(any_of(cont_vars), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))
    key <- paste(tr, "-", m)
    model_list[[key]] <- lmer(model_forms[[m]], data = df_sub, REML = TRUE)
    model_n[[key]] <- tibble(model = key, n_days = n_distinct(df_sub$Date), n_obs = nrow(df_sub),
                             first_day = min(df_sub$Date), last_day = max(df_sub$Date))
  }
}

# Sample size, period and R2 of each model (marginal = fixed effects; conditional = + random).
# A singular fit (a random-effect variance of 0) makes the conditional R2 unreliable.
purrr::imap_dfr(model_list, function(mod, key) {
  r2 <- r.squaredGLMM(mod)
  model_n[[key]] %>% mutate(r2_marginal = round(r2[1], 3), r2_conditional = round(r2[2], 3),
                            singular = isSingular(mod))
}) %>% print(width = Inf)

# Residual checks: residuals vs fitted (constant spread) and histogram (approximate normality).
res_df <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_list, ~ tibble(Fitted = fitted(.x), Residuals = resid(.x), model = .y))

resid_fitted_plot <- ggplot(res_df, aes(Fitted, Residuals)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ model, scales = "free") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
print(resid_fitted_plot)

hist_resi_plot <- ggplot(res_df, aes(Residuals)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "grey70", colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ model, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Histogram of model residuals") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
print(hist_resi_plot)

# Fixed effects with 95% CIs; bars coloured when the CI excludes zero.
effect_df <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_list, function(mod, key) {
  tidy(mod, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    mutate(Treatment = sub(" - .*", "", key), model = sub(".* - ", "", key),
           Sig = conf.low * conf.high > 0)
})

mml_plot <- ggplot(effect_df, aes(x = reorder(term, estimate), y = estimate,
                                  fill = ifelse(Sig, Treatment, "grey70"))) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), width = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_grid(Treatment ~ model) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(treatment_colors, "grey70" = "grey70")) +
  labs(x = "Predictor", y = "Effect size (SD units)") +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(),
        text = element_text(size = 14), legend.position = "none")
print(mml_plot)
ggsave("fig_S2_mixed_model.png", mml_plot, width = 11, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# Table: four columns (treatment x model). Labels are matched by term name, so the
# missing SapFlow row in model A does not shift the labels.
rmle_results <- tab_model(
  model_list,
    # The N per group printed by tab_model is wrong when models have different days;
  # the real number of days per model is in the table printed above (n_days).
  show.se = TRUE, show.ci = 0.95, show.re.var = TRUE, show.icc = TRUE, show.r2 = TRUE,
  show.ngroups = FALSE,
  dv.labels = names(model_list),
  pred.labels = c(`(Intercept)` = "(Intercept)", Temp = "Temperature", SWC = "SWC",
                  GWL = "Groundwater level", VPD = "VPD", SapFlow = "Sap flow", Rain = "Rain"))
print(rmle_results)
```

# Setup df for analysis: water table, transpiration, SWC and CH4 data

```{r}

#   Parameters, helper functions and the daily tables used by all following
#   chunks: weather (met_daily), soil moisture (swc_daily) and CH4 (ch4_all).
p_load(nlme, ranger, zoo, janitor, MODISTools, mgcv)

# Periods 
study_start  <- as.POSIXct("2024-04-05 15:00:00") # first and last flux measurements (hourly data)
study_end    <- as.POSIXct("2025-01-14 16:00:00")
win_start    <- as_date(study_start)               # same period as dates, for daily tables
win_end      <- as_date(study_end)
data_start   <- as.Date("2024-03-25")   # longer period for the wells and the water-balance model
data_end     <- as.Date("2025-05-15")
leafon_start <- as.Date("2024-05-20")              # leaf-on window (fixed dates)
leafon_end   <- as.Date("2024-10-15")

# Data-quality thresholds
tr_floor    <- -0.49   # TR water-level sensor at ~0.50 m: values at or below are censored
sap_max     <- 0.1     # sap flux at or above this value is a sensor error
swc_min     <- 0.05    # SWC below this value is a sensor error
ts_frozen   <- 0       # days with soil temperature at or below 0 C are excluded (frozen soil)
min_obs_day <- 4       # minimum SWC measurements per port and day
rain_min_mm <- 1       # rain-free day: less than 1 mm

# Random forest settings
cv_block_days <- 14    # length of the blocks held out in cross-validation (days)
n_trees       <- 500

# Site 
noaa_station <- "9063079"            # NOAA Marblehead, OH (Lake Erie level)
site_lat     <- 41.378165
site_lon     <- -82.508944

treatment_colors <- c("Control" = "#7AD151FF", "Root-free" = "#440154FF")
well_colors      <- c("TR" = "#7AD151FF", "WTE" = "#2A788EFF", "W" = "#440154FF")

# Helper functions
# Mean of the last k days, using measured days only.
# NA when fewer than min_frac of the k days have data (no gap filling).
roll_mean_obs <- function(x, k, min_frac = 0.8) {
  zoo::rollapplyr(x, k, function(v) {
    if (length(v) < k || sum(!is.na(v)) < min_frac * k) NA_real_ else mean(v, na.rm = TRUE)
  }, partial = TRUE, fill = NA)
}

# Sum of the last k days; NA unless every day in the window was measured.
roll_sum_obs <- function(x, k) {
  zoo::rollapplyr(x, k, function(v) if (length(v) < k || anyNA(v)) NA_real_ else sum(v),
                  partial = TRUE, fill = NA)
}

# Standardize to mean 0 and SD 1 (constant or empty vectors return NA).
z <- function(x) {
  s <- sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(s) || s == 0) return(rep(NA_real_, length(x)))
  (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / s
}

# Daily weather
# From df_L1_root (one record per hour), not from df_L1_datetime, which only
# has rows for hours with sap-flow records and would miss rain.
met_daily <- df_L1_root %>%
  mutate(DATE = as_date(datetime)) %>%
  group_by(DATE) %>%
  summarise(rain    = sum(rain_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_hours = sum(!is.na(rain_sum)),
            vpd_max = suppressWarnings(max(VPD_hour, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(rain    = if_else(n_hours >= 20, rain, NA_real_),       # incomplete days -> NA
         vpd_max = if_else(is.finite(vpd_max), vpd_max, NA_real_)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-n_hours)

# Check: total rain and incomplete days in the study period
# (df_L1_root ends on 2024-12-31, so 1-14 Jan 2025 have no weather data)
met_daily %>%
  filter(DATE >= win_start, DATE <= win_end) %>%
  summarise(total_rain_mm = sum(rain, na.rm = TRUE), days_without_rain_data = sum(is.na(rain))) %>%
  print()

# Daily SWC per port
# Median of the day; drops SWC sensor errors, days with few measurements and frozen soil.
swc_daily <- L1_flux %>%
  filter(datetime >= study_start, datetime <= study_end) %>%
  mutate(DATE  = as_date(datetime),
         SWC_1 = if_else(SWC_1 < swc_min, NA_real_, SWC_1)) %>%
  group_by(DATE, PORT, Treat) %>%
  summarise(swc    = median(SWC_1, na.rm = TRUE),
            ts_min = suppressWarnings(min(TS_1, na.rm = TRUE)),
            n_obs  = sum(is.finite(SWC_1)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_obs >= min_obs_day, !is.finite(ts_min) | ts_min > ts_frozen) %>%
  mutate(PORT  = factor(PORT),
         Treat = factor(Treat, levels = c("Control", "Root-free")))

# Daily CH4 per port
# Median flux and soil temperature of the day, kept only on days with valid SWC.
ch4_all <- L1_flux %>%
  filter(datetime >= study_start, datetime <= study_end) %>%
  mutate(DATE = as_date(datetime), PORT = factor(PORT)) %>%
  group_by(DATE, PORT) %>%
  summarise(fch4 = median(FCH4, na.rm = TRUE),
            ts   = median(TS_1, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  inner_join(swc_daily %>% dplyr::select(DATE, PORT, Treat, swc), by = c("DATE", "PORT")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(fch4), !is.na(ts))
```

# Drivers: sap flux, MODIS GPP, Lake Erie 

```{r}
# Lake Erie level from NOAA (one request per month; IGLD datum, local standard time).
# Downloaded once and saved, so rendering does not depend on the NOAA server.
get_noaa_level <- function(station, start, end) {
  months <- seq(floor_date(start, "month"), floor_date(end, "month"), by = "month")
  purrr::map_dfr(months, function(m) {
    url <- paste0("https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/api/prod/datagetter?",
                  "product=hourly_height&station=", station,
                  "&begin_date=", format(m, "%Y%m%d"),
                  "&end_date=", format(ceiling_date(m, "month") - days(1), "%Y%m%d"),
                  "&datum=IGLD&units=metric&time_zone=lst&format=csv&application=OWC_root_exclusion")
    out <- tryCatch(clean_names(read_csv(url, show_col_types = FALSE)), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(out) || !"water_level" %in% names(out)) return(NULL)   # month not available
    tibble(datetime   = if (inherits(out$date_time, "POSIXct")) out$date_time else ymd_hm(out$date_time),
           lake_level = as.numeric(out$water_level))
  })
}

lake_file <- dfile("lake_level_hourly_2024_2025.rds", must_exist = FALSE)
if (!file.exists(lake_file)) saveRDS(get_noaa_level(noaa_station, data_start - 40, data_end), lake_file)

lake_d <- readRDS(lake_file) %>%
  group_by(DATE = as_date(datetime)) %>%
  summarise(lake = mean(lake_level, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(lake_change = lake - lag(lake))   # daily change, used to test external control of the water table

# Sap flux of the TR trees. df_sap_OWC is already hourly, restricted to TR and the
# study period, with the unreliable months removed ("Preparing df's").
# F is Granier sap flux density at the sensor (per unit sapwood area); it is NOT scaled
# to tree or stand sapwood area. sap_mid (midday median, 11-14 h) is the transpiration
# proxy used in the models (standardized, so its units do not matter there).
# sap_sum (daily integral of F) is only meaningful for a stand water balance after unit
# conversion and scaling by sapwood area per ground area (not yet available).
sap_d <- df_sap_OWC %>%
  mutate(F = if_else(F >= sap_max, NA_real_, F),
         DATE = as_date(datetime), hr = hour(datetime)) %>%
  group_by(DATE, Sensor_ID) %>%
  summarise(sap_mid = median(F[hr %in% 11:14], na.rm = TRUE),
            sap_sum = sum(F, na.rm = TRUE) * 3600,
            n_hours = sum(is.finite(F)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_hours >= 20, is.finite(sap_mid)) %>%
  group_by(DATE) %>%         # median across sensors: robust to one bad sensor
  summarise(sap_mid = median(sap_mid), sap_sum = median(sap_sum), .groups = "drop")

# MODIS GPP (MOD17A2HGF, 500 m pixel). Each value is an 8-day composite, so each day
# takes the value of the composite it belongs to (no interpolation between composites).
# Values above 32760 are MODIS fill codes; scale 0.0001 kg C m-2 per 8 days -> g C m-2 d-1.
gpp_file     <- dfile("modis_gpp_OWC_8day_2024_2025.rds", must_exist = FALSE)   # dated at the composite start
gpp_file_old <- dfile("modis_gpp_OWC_2024_2025.rds", must_exist = FALSE) # earlier download, dated at the midpoint (start + 4 d)

if (!file.exists(gpp_file) && file.exists(gpp_file_old)) {
  readRDS(gpp_file_old) %>% mutate(DATE = DATE - 4) %>% saveRDS(gpp_file)   # reuse, no new download
}
if (!file.exists(gpp_file)) {
  mt_subset(product = "MOD17A2HGF", band = "Gpp_500m", lat = site_lat, lon = site_lon,
            start = as.character(data_start - 40), end = as.character(data_end),
            km_lr = 0, km_ab = 0, site_name = "OWC", internal = TRUE, progress = FALSE) %>%
    transmute(DATE = as_date(calendar_date),
              gpp  = if_else(value > 32760, NA_real_, value * 0.0001 * 1000 / 8)) %>%
    saveRDS(gpp_file)
}

# Daily driver table. Starts 40 days before the wells so the 30-day windows are
# complete at the start of the record. Rain windows are sums of complete windows only;
# sap flux and GPP windows are means of the measured days (>= 80% of the window).
drivers_all <- tibble(DATE = seq(data_start - 40, data_end, by = "day")) %>%
  left_join(met_daily, by = "DATE") %>%
  left_join(lake_d, by = "DATE") %>%
  left_join(sap_d, by = "DATE") %>%
  left_join(readRDS(gpp_file), by = "DATE") %>%
  tidyr::fill(gpp, .direction = "down") %>%
  mutate(rain_7d   = roll_sum_obs(rain, 7),
         rain_30d  = roll_sum_obs(rain, 30),
         sap_cum30 = roll_mean_obs(sap_mid, 30),
         gpp_cum30 = roll_mean_obs(gpp, 30))
```

# Standing transpiration
```{r}
# Stand transpiration of the TR plot (mm d-1): sap flux density scaled by sapwood area.
# Placed right after "Drivers": it adds E_mm and E_mean30 to drivers_all, so the later
# chunks can use transpiration in water units, not only the standardized proxy.
#
# Steps: (1) sapwood area of every live tree in the plot (2024 census); (2) daily sap flux
# density as the median of the sensors; (3) stand transpiration = flux density x sapwood
# area per ground area. Only measured days are used (no gap filling).
#
# Assumptions to state in Methods:
#   - All trees in the TR plot are treated as oaks (Quercus); the inventory has no species,
#     so the oak sapwood allometry and the oak sap flux sensors represent the whole stand.
#   - F is Granier sap flux density in cm3 cm-2 s-1 (0.0119 * K^1.231); change f_to_cm_s otherwise.
#   - No radial or probe-in-heartwood correction (Clearwater et al. 1999). Oak sapwood here
#     (16-47 mm) is often thinner than the probe, so E is likely underestimated (lower bound).

plot_area_m2 <- 625                    # TR inventory plot area (m2): confirm
f_to_cm_s    <- 1                     # multiplier converting F to cm3 cm-2 s-1
dead_codes   <- c("D", "DS", "DN")    # Status_2024 codes of dead trees (LI = live)

# (1a) Oak sapwood allometry from the cores. Sapwood area is the outer ring of the stem,
# pi * (r^2 - (r - s)^2), with r = DBH / 2 and s = sapwood depth.
ring_area_cm2 <- function(dbh_m, depth_mm) {
  r <- dbh_m * 100 / 2
  pi * (r^2 - pmax(r - depth_mm / 10, 0)^2)
}

# The core file has a title line ("Nate Mcdowell coastal dieback cores") above the header,
# so the header is found as the first line containing "genus". cores_file holds only the
# path (text); the table goes to cores_raw, so readLines() never receives a table.
# All columns are read as text; janitor standardizes names ("DBH (m) field" -> dbh_m_field).
cores_file <- dfile("bai_data_OWC.csv")
header_row <- which(str_detect(tolower(readLines(cores_file, warn = FALSE)), "genus"))[1]
if (is.na(header_row)) stop("No line containing 'genus' in ", cores_file)
cores_raw <- read_csv(cores_file, skip = header_row - 1,
                      col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names()
needed_cols <- c("genus", "dbh_m_field", "sapwood_msmt_mm")
if (!all(needed_cols %in% names(cores_raw)))
  stop("Core file columns differ from the expected ones. Found: ", paste(names(cores_raw), collapse = ", "),
       "\nRename them in the transmute() below.")
cores <- cores_raw %>%
  transmute(genus,
            dbh_field_m = readr::parse_number(dbh_m_field),       # m
            sapwood_mm  = readr::parse_number(sapwood_msmt_mm)) %>% # mm
  filter(str_detect(genus, regex("^qu", ignore_case = TRUE)), !is.na(dbh_field_m), !is.na(sapwood_mm)) %>%
  mutate(sapwood_cm2 = ring_area_cm2(dbh_field_m, sapwood_mm))
oak_allom <- lm(log(sapwood_cm2) ~ log(dbh_field_m * 100), data = cores)
message(nrow(cores), " oak cores used for the sapwood allometry")
print(summary(oak_allom)$coefficients)

# (1b) Sapwood area of every live tree in the plot. All columns are read as text because
# read_csv guesses types from the first rows and can turn later values into NA.
inventory <- read_csv(dfile("LE_TreePlotInventory_OWC.csv"),
                      col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) %>%
  filter(Site == "OWC", Plot == "TR") %>%
  transmute(tree_id = Tag, status = Status_2024,
            dbh_m   = readr::parse_number(DBH_cm_2024) / 100) %>%
  filter(!is.na(dbh_m), !status %in% dead_codes) %>%
  mutate(sapwood_cm2 = exp(predict(oak_allom, newdata = data.frame(dbh_field_m = dbh_m))))

# Sapwood area per ground area. Forests usually have ~5-40 cm2 m-2; a much larger value
# points to a wrong plot area.
as_ag_cm2_per_m2 <- sum(inventory$sapwood_cm2) / plot_area_m2
message(nrow(inventory), " live trees | sapwood area per ground area: ", round(as_ag_cm2_per_m2, 1), " cm2 m-2",
        if (as_ag_cm2_per_m2 > 60) " -> unusually high, check plot_area_m2" else "")

# (2) Daily sap flux density per sensor, complete days only (>= 20 measured hours), then
# the median across sensors. df_sap_OWC already has the unreliable periods removed.
js_daily <- df_sap_OWC %>%
  filter(!is.na(F), F < sap_max) %>%
  group_by(DATE = as_date(datetime), Sensor_ID) %>%
  summarise(js = sum(F * f_to_cm_s) * 3600, n_hours = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%   # cm3 cm-2 d-1
  filter(n_hours >= 20) %>%
  group_by(DATE) %>%
  summarise(js = median(js), n_sensors = n(), .groups = "drop")

# (3) Stand transpiration. Sapwood per ground area / 1e4 -> cm2 cm-2; 1 cm3 of water per
# cm2 of ground = 10 mm.
E_stand <- js_daily %>%
  transmute(DATE, E_mm = js * as_ag_cm2_per_m2 / 1e4 * 10, n_sensors)

E_stand %>%
  filter(DATE >= leafon_start, DATE <= leafon_end) %>%
  summarise(days_measured = n(), E_mean_mm_d = mean(E_mm),
            E_p10 = quantile(E_mm, 0.1), E_p90 = quantile(E_mm, 0.9)) %>%
  print()

# Add to the driver table: daily E and its 30-day mean (measured days only, >= 80% of the window).
drivers_all <- drivers_all %>%
  dplyr::select(-any_of(c("E_mm", "E_mean30"))) %>%
  left_join(E_stand %>% dplyr::select(DATE, E_mm), by = "DATE") %>%
  mutate(E_mean30 = roll_mean_obs(E_mm, 30))
```

# Water level in the TR, WTE, e W
```{r}
# COMPASS L2 water-level files (parquet), one per plot, year and variable.
files <- list.files(compass_dir, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE,
                    pattern = "^OWC_(TR|W|WTE)_(2024|2025)_(gw-pressure-vented|gw-density).*parquet$")
message(length(files), " well files")
if (length(files) == 0) stop("No well files in ", compass_dir, ": check compass_dir in 'Initializing'")

# Well geometry (copy of the COMPASS Google Sheet in the repository).
# Sensor depth below the ground = ring-to-sensor length minus the well stick-up above the ground.
well_dimensions <- read_csv(dfile("well_dimensions.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(Site = site,
            Plot = case_when(transect_location == "Upland"     ~ "UP",
                             transect_location == "Transition" ~ "TR",
                             transect_location == "WTE"        ~ "WTE",
                             transect_location == "Wetland"    ~ "W"),
            ground_to_sensor_cm = ring_to_pressure_sensor_cm - (well_top_to_ground_cm - bolt_to_cap_cm))

# Water level relative to the ground surface (negative = below ground).
# Pressure (mbar) -> water column (m) using the measured water density; densities
# below 0.95 g cm-3 are not physical for water and are replaced by 1.
dat_L1_hour <- purrr::map_dfr(files, arrow::read_parquet) %>%
  group_by(TIMESTAMP, Site, Plot, research_name) %>%
  summarise(Value = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%   # one value per timestamp
  pivot_wider(names_from = research_name, values_from = Value) %>%
  left_join(well_dimensions, by = c("Site", "Plot")) %>%
  mutate(density = if_else(`gw-density` > 0.95, `gw-density`, 1),
         wl_below_surface_m = (`gw-pressure-vented` * 100) / (density * 1000 * 9.80665) -
           ground_to_sensor_cm / 100) %>%
  filter(as_date(TIMESTAMP) >= data_start, as_date(TIMESTAMP) < data_end) %>%
  dplyr::select(TIMESTAMP, Plot, wl_below_surface_m)

# Barrier beach open periods (OWC NERR daily log). When open, the estuary drains to the lake.
barrier_open <- tibble::tribble(
  ~start,       ~end,
  "2024-04-01", "2024-04-25",
  "2024-04-30", "2024-05-07",
  "2024-05-18", "2024-05-26",
  "2024-06-06", "2024-06-07",
  "2024-07-08", "2024-07-09",
  "2024-12-11", "2025-03-26",
  "2025-03-28", "2025-04-30",
  "2025-05-04", "2025-05-14") %>%
  mutate(xmin = as.POSIXct(start, tz = lubridate::tz(dat_L1_hour$TIMESTAMP)),          # for the figure
         xmax = as.POSIXct(end,   tz = lubridate::tz(dat_L1_hour$TIMESTAMP)) + days(1))

barrier_days <- barrier_open %>%                                                       # one row per open day
  reframe(DATE = seq(as.Date(start), as.Date(end), by = "day"), .by = start) %>%
  distinct(DATE) %>%
  mutate(barrier = "open")

fig_wells <- ggplot(dat_L1_hour, aes(TIMESTAMP, wl_below_surface_m, colour = Plot)) +
  geom_rect(data = barrier_open, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = well_colors) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Water level relative to ground surface (m)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Shaded: barrier beach open") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "top", text = element_text(size = 14))
print(fig_wells)

# Daily mean water level per well (one column per well), with every day present
# so lagged differences in the water-balance model refer to consecutive days.
wells_daily <- dat_L1_hour %>%
  group_by(DATE = as_date(TIMESTAMP), Plot) %>%
  summarise(wl = mean(wl_below_surface_m, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(wl = if_else(is.finite(wl), wl, NA_real_)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Plot, values_from = wl) %>%
  tidyr::complete(DATE = seq(data_start, data_end - 1, by = "day")) %>%
  left_join(barrier_days, by = "DATE") %>%
  mutate(barrier = factor(coalesce(barrier, "closed"), levels = c("open", "closed")))
```


# TR water-balance model for gap filling gwl <0.5m (supplementary)

```{r}
# Daily water balance of the shallow aquifer under TR, used to estimate the TR GW 
# level on days when it was below the sensor (censored) or missing:
#
#   dTR_t = a * rain_t - b * (TR_{t-1} - WTE_{t-1}) - c * ET_t + d
#
# a = rise per mm of rain (its inverse is the specific yield); b = lateral exchange with
# the downslope well (Darcy: flow proportional to the head difference); c = drawdown per
# unit of the transpiration proxy; d = constant. The unknown ground-elevation difference
# between the wells is constant, so it is absorbed by d and no survey is needed.

et_proxy      <- "gpp"   # GPP covers Nov-Jan; sap flux is missing there
exchange_with <- "WTE"   # nearest downslope well
n_sims        <- 500     # ensemble size for the uncertainty interval
res_block     <- 7       # residuals are resampled in 7-day blocks to keep their autocorrelation
set.seed(42)

# Daily table. tr_obs marks days with TR above its sensor (a real measurement).
# The head difference uses the previous day, because flow on day t depends on the
# gradient at the start of the day.
wb_daily <- wells_daily %>%
  left_join(met_daily %>% dplyr::select(DATE, rain), by = "DATE") %>%
  left_join(drivers_all %>% dplyr::select(DATE, sap_mid, gpp), by = "DATE") %>%
  mutate(down      = .data[[exchange_with]],
         et        = .data[[et_proxy]],
         tr_obs    = !is.na(TR) & TR > tr_floor,
         dTR       = TR - lag(TR),
         grad_prev = lag(TR) - lag(down),
         fit_ok    = tr_obs & lag(tr_obs))   # daily change only when both days were measured

# Fit on measured changes only. m_hydro (rain + exchange) and m_full (+ transpiration
# proxy) are compared to see whether the proxy adds information to the daily balance.
fit_df  <- wb_daily %>% filter(fit_ok, !is.na(rain), !is.na(grad_prev), !is.na(et))
m_hydro <- lm(dTR ~ rain + grad_prev, data = fit_df)
m_full  <- lm(dTR ~ rain + grad_prev + et, data = fit_df)

cat("Fitting days:", nrow(fit_df), "|", format(min(fit_df$DATE)), "to", format(max(fit_df$DATE)), "\n")
print(summary(m_full)$coefficients)
print(anova(m_hydro, m_full))

# Physical check of the fitted coefficients: specific yield (rise of a per mm of rain),
# time to equilibrate with the downslope well, and the ground-elevation difference implied by d.
cf <- coef(m_full)
tibble(specific_yield           = 0.001 / cf[["rain"]],
       exchange_time_days       = -1 / cf[["grad_prev"]],
       implied_dz_TR_minus_WTE_m = cf[["(Intercept)"]] / cf[["grad_prev"]]) %>%
  print()

# Forward simulation: on measured days the series restarts from the observation;
# on censored or missing days it is advanced with the water balance. Days without
# rain or downslope data keep the previous value.
simulate_tr <- function(df, cf, noise = rep(0, nrow(df))) {
  a <- cf[["rain"]]; b <- -cf[["grad_prev"]]; d <- cf[["(Intercept)"]]
  c_et <- if ("et" %in% names(cf)) -cf[["et"]] else 0
  sim <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(df))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(df))) {
    if (df$tr_obs[i]) { sim[i] <- df$TR[i]; next }
    if (i == 1 || is.na(sim[i - 1])) next
    if (anyNA(c(df$rain[i], df$down[i - 1]))) { sim[i] <- sim[i - 1]; next }
    et_i <- if (is.na(df$et[i])) 0 else df$et[i]
    sim[i] <- sim[i - 1] + a * df$rain[i] - b * (sim[i - 1] - df$down[i - 1]) - c_et * et_i + d + noise[i]
  }
  sim
}

# Uncertainty: each run draws the coefficients from their estimated covariance (parameter
# uncertainty) and adds resampled daily residuals (process uncertainty), so the interval
# widens with the time since the last measurement.
block_noise <- function(res, n, block) {
  starts <- sample(seq_len(length(res) - block + 1), ceiling(n / block), replace = TRUE)
  unlist(lapply(starts, function(s) res[s:(s + block - 1)]))[seq_len(n)]
}
cf_draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(n_sims, coef(m_full), vcov(m_full))
ens <- vapply(seq_len(n_sims), function(k)
  simulate_tr(wb_daily, cf_draws[k, ], noise = block_noise(residuals(m_full), nrow(wb_daily), res_block)),
  numeric(nrow(wb_daily)))

# On censored days the water level is known to be at or below the sensor, so values
# above the floor are capped. Sensor gaps (no reading at all) are not capped.
censored_days <- !is.na(wb_daily$TR) & !wb_daily$tr_obs
p_above <- rowMeans(ens > tr_floor, na.rm = TRUE)     # share of runs above the floor
ens[censored_days, ] <- pmin(ens[censored_days, ], tr_floor)
q <- apply(ens, 1, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)

# Gap-filled series with flags: status of each day, median and 95% interval of the
# ensemble, whether the model wanted to put TR above the sensor (capped), whether the
# drivers were outside the range used to fit the model (out_of_range), and days since
# the last measurement.
rng <- function(x) range(x, na.rm = TRUE)
tr_filled <- wb_daily %>%
  dplyr::select(DATE, TR, tr_obs, rain, et, down) %>%
  mutate(status   = case_when(tr_obs ~ "observed",
                              !is.na(TR) ~ "censored (below sensor)",
                              TRUE ~ "missing (sensor gap)"),
         filled   = !tr_obs,
         TR_best  = if_else(tr_obs, TR, q[2, ]),
         TR_lwr   = if_else(tr_obs, TR, q[1, ]),
         TR_upr   = if_else(tr_obs, TR, q[3, ]),
         ci_width = TR_upr - TR_lwr,
         capped   = status == "censored (below sensor)" & p_above > 0.5,
         grad_sim = lag(TR_best) - lag(down),
         out_of_range = filled & (grad_sim < rng(fit_df$grad_prev)[1] | grad_sim > rng(fit_df$grad_prev)[2] |
                                  (!is.na(et) & (et < rng(fit_df$et)[1] | et > rng(fit_df$et)[2])) |
                                  rain > rng(fit_df$rain)[2])) %>%
  group_by(obs_grp = cumsum(tr_obs)) %>%
  mutate(days_since_obs = if_else(obs_grp == 0, NA_real_, as.numeric(row_number() - 1))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-obs_grp, -grad_sim)

# How much of the study period is filled, how much is extrapolated, and how uncertain.
study <- tr_filled %>% filter(DATE >= win_start, DATE <= win_end)
study %>%
  summarise(n_days             = n(),
            pct_observed       = round(100 * mean(status == "observed"), 1),
            pct_censored       = round(100 * mean(status == "censored (below sensor)"), 1),
            pct_missing        = round(100 * mean(status == "missing (sensor gap)"), 1),
            pct_out_of_range   = round(100 * mean(out_of_range, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            pct_capped         = round(100 * mean(capped, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            median_ci_width_m  = round(median(ci_width[filled], na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            max_days_since_obs = max(days_since_obs, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  print(width = Inf)

study %>%
  group_by(month = floor_date(DATE, "month")) %>%
  summarise(pct_filled       = round(100 * mean(filled)),
            pct_out_of_range = round(100 * mean(out_of_range, na.rm = TRUE)),
            pct_capped       = round(100 * mean(capped, na.rm = TRUE)),
            TR_best_median   = round(median(TR_best, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
            ci_width_median  = round(median(ci_width[filled], na.rm = TRUE), 3), .groups = "drop") %>%
  print(n = Inf)

fig_fill <- ggplot(tr_filled, aes(DATE)) +
  geom_rect(data = barrier_open, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(xmin = as.Date(start), xmax = as.Date(end) + 1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = leafon_start, xmax = leafon_end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#7AD151FF", alpha = 0.06) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = tr_floor, colour = "#7AD151FF", linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line(data = wells_daily, aes(y = W,   colour = "W"),   linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(data = wells_daily, aes(y = WTE, colour = "WTE"), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = if_else(filled, TR_lwr, NA_real_), ymax = if_else(filled, TR_upr, NA_real_)),
              fill = "grey40", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = if_else(filled, TR_best, NA_real_)), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(y = if_else(tr_obs, TR, NA_real_), colour = "TR"), size = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = filter(tr_filled, out_of_range), aes(y = TR_best),
             shape = 4, size = 1.2, colour = "firebrick") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = well_colors) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Water level relative to ground surface (m)", colour = NULL,
       caption = paste("TR filled: black line and grey band (median and 95% interval of", n_sims,
                       "runs); red x: drivers outside the fitted range; blue: barrier open; green: leaf-on")) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "top", text = element_text(size = 14))
print(fig_fill)
ggsave("fig_TR_gapfilled.png", fig_fill, width = 14, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```


# Transpiration vs water table: random forest partition (supplementary)

```{r}
# Random-forest partition of transpiration vs external hydrology (supplementary).
# Ben suggestion: quantify how much of the variation in the water table, soil moisture
# and CH4 is explained by transpiration and how much by external hydrology.
#
# Transpiration is represented only by its proxies (TR sap flux, MODIS GPP, plus VPD).
# External hydrology: rain, Lake Erie level, estuary water level (W well) and the TR water table.
#
# Method used for every question: random forests evaluated with blocked cross-validation
# (each 14-day block is predicted by a model trained without it, so autocorrelated
# neighbouring days never predict themselves). The cross-validated R2 is then split into
# the part only transpiration explains, the part only hydrology explains, and the part
# either can explain (shared, i.e. they vary together over the season).
#
# The TR water table enters in two versions: "filled" (gap-filled by the water-balance
# model; main) and "censored" (observed values capped at the sensor plus a flag for
# below-sensor days; sensitivity). The GPP term was not significant in the water-balance
# model, so the filled series contains little GPP information; comparing both versions
# checks that gap filling does not drive the results.

wt_versions <- c("filled", "censored")

# Daily water-table variables. dgwl_obs uses measured days only: simulated changes
# contain the model's own terms and cannot be used to test what drives the water table.
wt_daily <- tr_filled %>%
  dplyr::select(DATE, TR_obs = TR, tr_obs, status, gwl_fill = TR_best) %>%
  left_join(wells_daily %>% dplyr::select(DATE, W), by = "DATE") %>%
  mutate(gw_below  = as.integer(status == "censored (below sensor)"),
         gwl_cens  = if_else(is.na(TR_obs), NA_real_, pmax(TR_obs, tr_floor)),
         dgwl_obs  = if_else(tr_obs & lag(tr_obs), TR_obs - lag(TR_obs), NA_real_),
         dgwl_fill = gwl_fill - lag(gwl_fill),
         dgwl_cens = gwl_cens - lag(gwl_cens),
         dW        = W - lag(W))

drivers_wt <- drivers_all %>% left_join(wt_daily, by = "DATE")

# One value per treatment and day (median across the four ports), study period only.
resp_daily <- swc_daily %>%
  group_by(DATE, Treat) %>%
  summarise(swc = median(swc), .groups = "drop") %>%
  full_join(ch4_all %>%
              group_by(DATE, Treat) %>%
              summarise(fch4 = median(fch4), ts = median(ts), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("DATE", "Treat")) %>%
  left_join(drivers_wt, by = "DATE") %>%
  filter(DATE >= win_start, DATE <= win_end)

# How strongly the transpiration proxies covary with the water table (reported in Methods):
# high correlations are why part of the variance cannot be attributed to either driver.
drivers_wt %>%
  filter(DATE >= win_start, DATE <= win_end) %>%
  summarise(r_sapcum_gwlfill = cor(sap_cum30, gwl_fill, use = "complete.obs"),
            r_gppcum_gwlfill = cor(gpp_cum30, gwl_fill, use = "complete.obs"),
            r_sapcum_gwlcens = cor(sap_cum30, gwl_cens, use = "complete.obs"),
            r_gppcum_gwlcens = cor(gpp_cum30, gwl_cens, use = "complete.obs"),
            r_sap_gpp        = cor(sap_mid, gpp, use = "complete.obs")) %>%
  print()

# Predictor groups. Water-table levels explain levels (SWC, CH4); water-table changes
# explain day-to-day changes (Q2b).
hydro_level  <- list(filled   = c("gwl_fill", "W", "rain_7d", "rain_30d", "lake"),
                     censored = c("gwl_cens", "gw_below", "W", "rain_7d", "rain_30d", "lake"))
hydro_change <- list(filled   = c("gwl_fill", "dgwl_fill", "dW", "rain_7d", "lake_change"),
                     censored = c("gwl_cens", "dgwl_cens", "gw_below", "dW", "rain_7d", "lake_change"))
proxies <- list("Sap flux"  = list(day = "sap_mid", cum = "sap_cum30"),
                "MODIS GPP" = list(day = "gpp",     cum = "gpp_cum30"))

# Blocked cross-validated R2 of a random forest; predictions worse than the mean count as 0.
cv_r2 <- function(d, response, preds) {
  folds <- as.integer(as.numeric(d$DATE - min(d$DATE)) %/% cv_block_days)
  pred  <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(d))
  for (f in unique(folds)) {
    train <- folds != f
    fit <- ranger::ranger(x = d[train, preds, drop = FALSE], y = d[[response]][train],
                          num.trees = n_trees, seed = 42)
    pred[!train] <- predict(fit, data = d[!train, preds, drop = FALSE])$predictions
  }
  obs <- d[[response]]
  max(0, 1 - sum((obs - pred)^2) / sum((obs - mean(obs))^2))
}

# Commonality partition: R2 with all predictors, without transpiration, without hydrology
# and with covariates only (all on the same days). Unique = R2 lost when a group is
# removed; shared = what either group explains alone; can be negative (suppression).
partition <- function(df, response, transp, hydro, base = character(0), label) {
  d <- df %>%
    dplyr::select(DATE, all_of(c(response, transp, hydro, base))) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na() %>%
    arrange(DATE) %>%
    as.data.frame()
  r2 <- function(p) if (length(p) == 0) 0 else cv_r2(d, response, p)
  full <- r2(c(transp, hydro, base)); no_transp <- r2(c(hydro, base))
  no_hydro <- r2(c(transp, base));     only_base <- r2(base)
  tibble(model = label, response = response, n_days = nrow(d),
         r2_full = full, unique_transp = full - no_transp, unique_hydro = full - no_hydro,
         shared = no_transp + no_hydro - only_base - full, covariates = only_base)
}

# Direction and size of effects: standardized GLS with temporal autocorrelation (CAR1).
gls_std <- function(d, resp, terms, label) {
  d <- d %>% dplyr::select(DATE, y = all_of(resp), all_of(terms)) %>% tidyr::drop_na() %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(terms), z), day_num = as.numeric(DATE - min(DATE)))
  m <- nlme::gls(reformulate(terms, "y"), correlation = nlme::corCAR1(form = ~ day_num),
                 data = d, control = nlme::glsControl(opt = "optim"))
  as.data.frame(summary(m)$tTable) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    transmute(model = label, term, estimate_per_sd = Value, se = Std.Error, p = `p-value`, n = nrow(d))
}

# Q1. Are daily changes in the TR water table driven by transpiration or by external hydrology?
# Response: measured day-to-day change of the TR water level (days above the sensor).
# Transpiration group: same-day proxy + VPD. Hydrology group: rain (day and 7 d),
# change in lake level and change in estuary level.
q1_df <- drivers_wt %>% filter(DATE >= win_start, DATE <= win_end)
q1 <- purrr::imap_dfr(proxies, function(p, pname)
  partition(q1_df, "dgwl_obs", transp = c(p$day, "vpd_max"),
            hydro = c("rain", "rain_7d", "lake_change", "dW"),
            label = paste("Water-level change |", pname)))
q1_coef <- purrr::imap_dfr(proxies, function(p, pname)
  gls_std(q1_df, "dgwl_obs", c(p$day, "rain", "lake_change", "dW"), paste("Water-level change |", pname)))
print(q1_coef)

# Q2. Is soil moisture explained by transpiration or by the water table?
# Response: daily SWC per treatment. Transpiration enters as the 30-day mean proxy
# (soil water is a store, depleted over weeks) plus the same-day proxy and VPD.
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(pname = names(proxies), trt = c("Control", "Root-free"), wt = wt_versions)
q2 <- purrr::pmap_dfr(grid, function(pname, trt, wt) {
  p <- proxies[[pname]]
  partition(filter(resp_daily, Treat == trt), "swc",
            transp = c(p$cum, p$day, "vpd_max"), hydro = hydro_level[[wt]],
            label = paste("SWC", trt, "|", pname, "| WT", wt))
})

# Q2b. On rain-free days, does soil moisture fall faster when trees transpire more?
# Day-to-day changes remove the seasonal trend that transpiration and the water table share.
dry_dates <- drivers_all %>% filter(rain < rain_min_mm, lag(rain) < rain_min_mm) %>% pull(DATE)
resp_change <- resp_daily %>%
  group_by(Treat) %>%
  arrange(DATE, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(dswc = if_else(as.numeric(DATE - lag(DATE)) == 1, swc - lag(swc), NA_real_)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(DATE %in% dry_dates)

q2b <- purrr::pmap_dfr(grid, function(pname, trt, wt) {
  p <- proxies[[pname]]
  partition(filter(resp_change, Treat == trt), "dswc",
            transp = c(p$day, "vpd_max"), hydro = hydro_change[[wt]],
            label = paste("SWC change (dry days)", trt, "|", pname, "| WT", wt))
})
q2b_coef <- tidyr::expand_grid(pname = names(proxies), wt = wt_versions) %>%
  purrr::pmap_dfr(function(pname, wt) {
    wt_terms <- if (wt == "filled") c("gwl_fill", "dgwl_fill") else c("gwl_cens", "dgwl_cens")
    gls_std(filter(resp_change, Treat == "Control"), "dswc",
            c(proxies[[pname]]$day, "vpd_max", wt_terms, "dW"),
            paste("SWC change Control |", pname, "| WT", wt))
  })
print(q2b_coef)

# Q3. How do transpiration and hydrology affect CH4 flux, and does it act through soil moisture?
# Soil temperature is a covariate in all models. Adding SWC as a covariate tests mediation:
# if the transpiration and hydrology parts vanish, their effect on CH4 passes through SWC.
q3 <- tidyr::expand_grid(grid, with_swc = c(FALSE, TRUE)) %>%
  purrr::pmap_dfr(function(pname, trt, wt, with_swc) {
    p <- proxies[[pname]]
    partition(filter(resp_daily, Treat == trt), "fch4",
              transp = c(p$cum, p$day, "vpd_max"), hydro = hydro_level[[wt]],
              base = if (with_swc) c("ts", "swc") else "ts",
              label = paste("CH4", trt, "|", pname, "| WT", wt, if (with_swc) "| + SWC" else ""))
  })

# Summary table of all partitions
partition_tbl <- bind_rows(q1, q2, q2b, q3) %>%
  mutate(wt_version = case_when(grepl("WT filled", model)   ~ "filled",
                                grepl("WT censored", model) ~ "censored",
                                TRUE                        ~ "observed changes"),
         across(c(r2_full, unique_transp, unique_hydro, shared, covariates), ~ round(.x, 3)))
print(partition_tbl, n = Inf, width = Inf)

# Figure: main version (measured changes for Q1, filled water table for Q2-Q3).
# Negative components (suppression) are drawn as zero.
fig_partition <- partition_tbl %>%
  filter(wt_version != "censored") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(unique_transp, shared, unique_hydro, covariates),
                      names_to = "component", values_to = "r2") %>%
  mutate(r2 = pmax(r2, 0),
         model = sub(" \\| WT filled", "", model),
         component = factor(component, levels = c("unique_transp", "shared", "unique_hydro", "covariates"),
                            labels = c("Transpiration (unique)", "Shared", "Hydrology (unique)",
                                       "Covariates (Ts, SWC)")),
         response = factor(response, levels = c("dgwl_obs", "swc", "dswc", "fch4"),
                           labels = c("Water-level change", "Soil moisture",
                                      "SWC change (dry days)", "CH4 flux"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(r2, model, fill = component)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(response ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Transpiration (unique)" = "#7AD151FF", "Shared" = "grey70",
                               "Hydrology (unique)" = "#2A788EFF", "Covariates (Ts, SWC)" = "#FDE725FF")) +
  labs(x = bquote("Cross-validated" ~ R^2 ~ "(blocked, 14-day blocks)"), y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       caption = "Water table: gap-filled TR (sensitivity with censored TR in Table SX)") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "top", text = element_text(size = 13))
print(fig_partition)
ggsave("fig_rf_partition_reviewer.png", fig_partition, width = 11, height = 11, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# Sensitivity: filled vs censored water table, side by side. Similar values mean the
# conclusions do not depend on gap filling.
partition_tbl %>%
  filter(wt_version %in% wt_versions) %>%
  mutate(model_base = sub(" \\| WT (filled|censored)", "", model)) %>%
  dplyr::select(model_base, wt_version, r2_full, unique_transp, unique_hydro, shared) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = wt_version, values_from = c(r2_full, unique_transp, unique_hydro, shared)) %>%
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

## Water table: transpiration vs external hydrology (censored regression)
```{r}
# Q5. Is the seasonal level of the TR water table set by transpiration or by external
# hydrology, using all days including those below the sensor?
#
# The TR water table was below its sensor (-0.49 m) on many leaf-on days. Dropping those
# days would remove exactly the period of interest, and gap filling would add model
# assumptions. Censored (Tobit) regression uses them as "at or below -0.49 m".
# External hydrology: estuary level (W well) and 30-day rain. Transpiration: the leaf-on
# window, the 30-day mean of sap flux (tree-specific), MODIS GPP and stand transpiration.
# 30-day mean VPD tests whether the drawdown follows atmospheric demand in general (which
# also drives soil evaporation and understory transpiration) or water use by the trees.
# 95% CIs from a 14-day moving-block bootstrap, which keeps the temporal autocorrelation.
p_load(AER, boot)

n_boot_tobit <- 1000
peak_start   <- as.Date("2024-07-15")   # peak leaf-on window for the seasonal contrast
peak_end     <- as.Date("2024-09-15")
sy           <- 0.001 / coef(m_full)[["rain"]]   # specific yield from the water-balance model

# Daily table. Censored days are set to the floor value; the Tobit model treats them as
# "at or below". Barrier variables test whether estuary drainage explains the drawdown.
tob_df <- wb_daily %>%
  dplyr::select(DATE, TR, W) %>%
  left_join(drivers_all %>% dplyr::select(DATE, rain_30d, vpd_max, sap_cum30, gpp_cum30, any_of("E_mean30")),
            by = "DATE") %>%
  left_join(barrier_days, by = "DATE") %>%
  mutate(barrier_open_d = as.integer(!is.na(barrier)),
         open_30d  = zoo::rollapplyr(barrier_open_d, 30, sum, partial = TRUE),
         vpd_cum30 = roll_mean_obs(vpd_max, 30),
         leaf      = factor(if_else(DATE >= leafon_start & DATE <= leafon_end, "leaf-on", "leaf-off"),
                            levels = c("leaf-off", "leaf-on")),
         TR_c      = pmax(TR, tr_floor)) %>%
  filter(DATE >= win_start, DATE <= win_end) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(TR_c, W, rain_30d) %>%
  mutate(sap_z = z(sap_cum30), gpp_z = z(gpp_cum30), vpd_z = z(vpd_cum30))

# How the proxies covary with each other and with the estuary (collinearity check).
tob_df %>%
  summarise(n_days = n(), n_censored = sum(TR_c <= tr_floor),
            r_sap_vpd = cor(sap_z, vpd_z, use = "complete.obs"),
            r_gpp_vpd = cor(gpp_z, vpd_z, use = "complete.obs"),
            r_sap_W   = cor(sap_z, W,     use = "complete.obs")) %>%
  print()

# AER::tobit evaluates the call inside the formula's environment, so that environment is
# pointed to the local data in every fit (otherwise the bootstrap cannot find the data).
fit_tobit <- function(form, d) {
  environment(form) <- environment()
  AER::tobit(form, left = tr_floor, data = d)
}

tob_boot <- function(form, data, R = n_boot_tobit) {
  data <- data %>% dplyr::select(DATE, all_of(all.vars(form))) %>% tidyr::drop_na() %>% arrange(DATE)
  fit  <- fit_tobit(form, data)
  set.seed(42)
  bt <- boot::tsboot(data, function(d) coef(fit_tobit(form, d)), R = R, l = 14, sim = "fixed")
  tibble(term = names(coef(fit)), estimate = unname(coef(fit)),
         ci_low  = apply(bt$t, 2, quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
         ci_high = apply(bt$t, 2, quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
         n_days = nrow(data), n_censored = sum(data$TR_c <= tr_floor))
}

# M1-M2: phenology (with and without barrier state). M3-M6: proxies (sap flux is only
# available Apr-Oct 2024). M7: stand transpiration in its own units (m per mm d-1).
tob_sap <- filter(tob_df, !is.na(sap_z))
models <- list(
  `M1 leaf-on window`    = list(TR_c ~ W * leaf + rain_30d, tob_df),
  `M2 leaf-on + barrier` = list(TR_c ~ W + leaf + rain_30d + barrier_open_d + open_30d, tob_df),
  `M3 MODIS GPP`         = list(TR_c ~ W + rain_30d + gpp_z, tob_df),
  `M4 sap flux`          = list(TR_c ~ W + rain_30d + sap_z, tob_sap),
  `M5 VPD only`          = list(TR_c ~ W + rain_30d + vpd_z, tob_sap),
  `M6 sap flux + VPD`    = list(TR_c ~ W + rain_30d + sap_z + vpd_z, tob_sap))
if ("E_mean30" %in% names(tob_df) && sum(!is.na(tob_df$E_mean30)) > 50) {
  models$`M7 stand transpiration` <- list(TR_c ~ W + rain_30d + E_mean30, filter(tob_df, !is.na(E_mean30)))
}

tob_tbl <- purrr::imap_dfr(models, function(m, name) tob_boot(m[[1]], m[[2]]) %>% mutate(model = name)) %>%
  filter(!term %in% c("(Intercept)", "Log(scale)")) %>%
  mutate(ci_excludes_0 = sign(ci_low) == sign(ci_high)) %>%
  relocate(model)
print(tob_tbl %>% mutate(across(c(estimate, ci_low, ci_high), ~ round(.x, 4))), n = Inf, width = Inf)

# Standardized effects in physical units: 1 SD of each proxy, and the effect per unit.
tob_tbl %>%
  inner_join(tibble(term = c("sap_z", "gpp_z", "vpd_z"),
                    sd = c(sd(tob_sap$sap_cum30, na.rm = TRUE), sd(tob_df$gpp_cum30, na.rm = TRUE),
                           sd(tob_sap$vpd_cum30, na.rm = TRUE)),
                    units = c("F units (30-d mean midday sap flux)", "g C m-2 d-1 (30-d mean GPP)",
                              "kPa (30-d mean daily max VPD)")), by = "term") %>%
  transmute(model, term, one_sd = signif(sd, 3), units, m_per_unit = signif(estimate / sd, 3),
            ci_low_unit = signif(ci_low / sd, 3), ci_high_unit = signif(ci_high / sd, 3)) %>%
  print(width = Inf)

# Leaf-on drawdown expressed as water removed from the shallow aquifer (m x Sy = water depth).
tob_tbl %>%
  filter(term == "leafleaf-on") %>%
  transmute(model, drawdown_m = round(estimate, 3),
            water_mm = round(estimate * sy * 1000, 1),
            water_mm_low = round(ci_low * sy * 1000, 1), water_mm_high = round(ci_high * sy * 1000, 1)) %>%
  print()

# Physical reference for M7 (rough): if a 30-day mean transpiration of 1 mm d-1 (30 mm of
# water) came entirely from the aquifer, the water table would drop 30 / (Sy * 1000) m.
# The ratio of the fitted slope to this value approximates the share drawn from the aquifer.
if ("M7 stand transpiration" %in% tob_tbl$model) {
  tob_tbl %>%
    filter(term == "E_mean30") %>%
    mutate(expected_if_all_from_aquifer = -30 / (sy * 1000),
           share_from_aquifer = estimate / expected_if_all_from_aquifer) %>%
    print(width = Inf)
}

# Contribution of each driver to the seasonal decline (spring vs peak leaf-on):
# coefficient x centred predictor, averaged over each window.
decompose_tobit <- function(form, d, transp_var, label) {
  d  <- d %>% dplyr::select(DATE, all_of(all.vars(form))) %>% tidyr::drop_na()
  cf <- coef(fit_tobit(form, d))
  d %>% transmute(DATE,
                  `External (estuary W)` = cf[["W"]] * (W - mean(W)),
                  `Rain (30 d)`          = cf[["rain_30d"]] * (rain_30d - mean(rain_30d)),
                  Transpiration          = cf[[transp_var]] * (.data[[transp_var]] - mean(.data[[transp_var]])),
                  model = label)
}
contrib <- bind_rows(decompose_tobit(TR_c ~ W + rain_30d + sap_z, tob_sap, "sap_z", "Sap flux"),
                     decompose_tobit(TR_c ~ W + rain_30d + gpp_z, tob_df,  "gpp_z", "MODIS GPP"))

contrib %>%
  mutate(window = case_when(DATE < leafon_start ~ "spring",
                            DATE >= peak_start & DATE <= peak_end ~ "peak")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(window)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`External (estuary W)`, `Rain (30 d)`, Transpiration),
                      names_to = "driver", values_to = "contribution") %>%
  group_by(model, driver, window) %>%
  summarise(mean_m = mean(contribution), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = window, values_from = mean_m) %>%
  mutate(change_m = peak - spring) %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  mutate(share_of_decline_pct = round(100 * pmin(change_m, 0) / sum(pmin(change_m, 0)))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
```
